info.desc: Automatic for the People is the eighth album by the American alternative rock band R.E.M., released in 1992 on Warner Bros. Records. While R.E.M. had intended to make a harder-rocking album after dealing primarily with acoustic based sounds on its previous record Out of Time (1991), the group eventually abandoned that goal and created an album that was musically subdued and dealt with mortality. Automatic for the People reached number two on the US album charts and yielded six singles. It was ranked #247 in Rolling Stone’s 500 Greatest Albums of All Time. podcast.body: This album completes what is commonly referred to as R.E.M.'s "great trilogy" under Warner Music, a series celebrated as one of the best trilogies in American music history. While some critics advocate for expanding this to a "quadrilogy" by including the *Document* album, these three records remain critically important for tracing the historical trajectory of music. podcast.body: This album featured the song "The Sidewinder Sleeps Tonight," which incorporated a fragment of Solomon Linda's melody, leading to legal action. "REM recorded a song called The Sidewinder Sleeps Tonight on their album Automatic to the People, a record we will definitely be talking about in 2026."

podcast.body: This album was placed on the CD player by Kurt Cobain in the early morning of April 5, 1994, shortly before he committed suicide. He turned down the sound on MTV, found nothing interesting, and then decided to play R.E.M.'s album. "So he turned down the sound and went over to the CD player where he loaded R.E.M.'s automatic for the people album and let it play."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album, released in 1992, is considered R.E.M.'s biggest, selling millions of copies and earning a Grammy nomination. Six of its twelve tracks were released as singles. The album's title, "Automatic for the People," was adopted from the motto of Weaver D's Delicious Fine Foods, a local restaurant on East Broad Street in Athens, Georgia. "Our biggest album was Automatic for the People from 1992."
